newsitem.title: USA: Fear of crime a big factor in gun ownership - study.
newsitem.headline: Fear of crime a big factor in gun ownership - study.

text.p: Nearly half of American firearm owners and most handgun owners buy them for protection against crime, a survey released on Monday said.
The study said on a typical day in the United States 1 million adults carry a gun with them and a further 2 million carry a firearm in their vehicle.
About a quarter of American adults own a firearm and ownership is most prevalent among middled-aged, middle-class whites from rural areas.

Where once most firearms were used to hunting, now most handgun owners and 46 percent of all gunowners said they possessed a weapon primarily for protection against criminals, said the National Survey of Private Ownership of Firearms, carried out for the Police Foundation by professors from Georgetown and Duke universities.
"The United States has become much more citified. A couple of generations away from the farm, people turn away from guns and look to other hobbies and activities," it said.

"At the same time the move to the city exposes people to a greater threat from other people and a greater concern about crime. So there is a countervailing trend of people buying a handgun for protection."
One of the more disturbing findings of the survey was that one in every five gun owners failed to follow safe storage procedure of keeping a gun locked and unloaded.
"The risks of an accident are superseded for many owners by the risk of being unprepared for an intruder," it said.
Among the other findings: an estimated 192 million guns are in private possession, about one third of them handguns.
Whites are more likely to own guns than blacks, and blacks more likely than Hispanics.
About 70 percent of handgun owners favoured registration but the idea of a ban on ownership was "very unpopular indeed."
